_: T-532 DRAFT: one INDEX entry per seasonal form (CONTENT voice), as split and measured (Index line 234px; routine pane 113px)

lines: Frost settles on it and it lets it stay.
It has not decided what to be. It waits
for the thaw to decide for it.
Something grows from the top of it every
spring. It does not know what. Nobody
has shown it yet.
It warms to whatever is near. In summer
that is everything, so it cannot tell
which thing it warmed to.
It keeps the leaves that land on it. It
did not choose them. They are filed as
its own.
Its chest lights blink a pattern nothing
else in the cold can read. Something on
runners blinks back.
Its lights blink faster in spring. The
answer comes from overhead, a little
late, in the same pattern.
In summer its lights are answered from
the water. The pattern has no grammar
anyone else has written down.
Its lights blink across a field and are
answered from somewhere moving. Nobody
else knows what was agreed.
Ranges every track in reach and some
that are not. Finds the nearest field.
Nearest is not the same as right.
It keeps to tracks it has already made.
The snow fills the others in. It finds
the nearest one still there.
Comes back from every outing in mud. It
was looking for something it had seen
before. It found something close.
In summer it ranges the dry tracks and
comes back dusty. Asked what it found,
it names the nearest thing.
Floats on two hulls and takes everyone
who fits. Reads the water before it
reads the problem. Often correct.
Its floats freeze in and it stays put.
It keeps the canopy folded and the room
warm. Nobody asks how.
Sets out at the first thaw. Turns back
for anyone left on the shore. Cannot
say why it turned.
Takes the last trips of the year slowly.
Leaves land on its deck and it lets
them ride.
Flies circles over one field on a line
held from below. Sees the field very
clearly. Has never seen the line.
Climbs while the light holds. All it
was pointed at is recorded. The record
calls it very clear.
Flies low in autumn, under the wind. It
records the leaves. It has never
recorded the tree.
Lands on skis and waits for a still day.
It has never once turned round. The
lake is behind it.
Crosses the frozen lake at speed, its
screen up. Its track covers the last
one. What is covered goes on.
Its runners drip. It covers the thaw for
as long as it can. What it covers is
not removed.
Keeps its runners off the hot ground
and its screen dark. It is not hiding.
It is waiting for the cold.
Watches the first frost from under its
screen. It knows before anyone what
the lake will do.
Words only its own
family can follow.
It hits harder for
each of them near.
A tongue that only
its own kind speaks.
Each one in the
party adds to it.
